name: main
prose: Entry point of gensnmptree. Precondition: argc and argv are the process arguments. It loops over getopt with the option string "dEeFfhI:i:lp:t": -d sets the debug flag; -E, -e and -t choose the operation (OP_ENUMS, OP_EXTRACT, OP_TREE; the default is OP_GEN) and call errx(1) if an incompatible operation was already chosen (-t is accepted only after OP_GEN or OP_TREE); -F and -f choose GEN_FUNCS_C or GEN_FUNCS_H and call errx(1) if the other one was already chosen; -h writes the usage text to stderr and calls exit(0); -I calls path_new(optarg); -i records the input file name; -l sets localincs; -p records the file prefix and calls errx(1) if strlen(prefix) + strlen("tree.c") exceeds MAXPATHLEN. An unknown option letter has no case in the switch (getopt itself prints a diagnostic) and parsing just continues. It then reads the input from stdin, or from the -i file (err(1) if fopen fails), parses the first top-level construct with parse_top(gettoken()), merges every further construct into root until TOK_EOF, calls check_tree(root) only if root is non-NULL, and dispatches on op: OP_EXTRACT calls errx(1) when no operands remain, otherwise calls gen_extract(stdout, root, argv[i]) for each operand and calls errx(1) at the first operand for which it returns non-zero, else returns 0; OP_ENUMS calls make_enums(argc, argv, gen_funcs) and returns 0; OP_TREE calls errx(1) if operands remain, else gen_tree(root, 0) and returns 0; OP_GEN calls errx(1) if operands remain, else make_table(root, gen_funcs == GEN_FUNCS_H) and returns 0. The switch has no default case. The callees (parse_top, merge, check_tree, gen_*) may themselves terminate the process; they were not read in detail.
note: Reviewer claim 2 (OP_EXTRACT uses extract_enum) is wrong: gensnmptree.c main calls gen_extract(stdout, root, argv[i]) in the OP_EXTRACT case (the extract_enum calls are in make_enums). Claim 1 (check_tree only if root non-NULL) is right and already reflected. Real prose error found by hand: invalid options do not errx(1) (no '?' case in the switch).

name: snmp_set
prose: SET request processor of the SNMP agent library. Precondition: pdu is a parsed SET request whose nbindings does not exceed SNMP_MAX_BINDINGS (the local context arrays node[] and scratch[] are sized by it), resp is a PDU to fill, resp_b the output buffer, data the caller's context pointer. Steps: it builds the response header with snmp_pdu_create_response and snmp_pdu_encode_header; if the header cannot be encoded it returns SNMP_RET_IGN at once, without freeing resp, without touching pdu->error_status/error_index and without calling snmp_dep_finish. Phase 1, for each binding: find_node must find a node (otherwise error_index = i+1 and error_status is SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME for SNMPv1, else SNMP_ERR_NOT_WRITEABLE if find_subnode finds an intermediate node, SNMP_ERR_NO_ACCESS if the exception is SNMP_SYNTAX_NOSUCHOBJECT, otherwise SNMP_ERR_NO_CREATION); a leaf without SNMP_NODE_CANSET gives NOSUCHNAME (v1) or NOT_WRITEABLE; a syntax mismatch gives BADVALUE (v1) or WRONG_TYPE; a failed snmp_value_copy gives GENERR; a binding that cannot be encoded gives TOOBIG (ASN_ERR_EOBUF) or GENERR. Each of these failures sets error_index = i+1, calls snmp_pdu_free(resp) and returns SNMP_RET_ERR. Phase 2 calls the node's SET action for each binding (context.ctx.code starts as SNMP_RET_OK); for SNMPv1 several error codes are mapped to BADVALUE, NOSUCHNAME or GENERR; the first non-zero result sets error_index = i+1 and error_status = that code, calls rollback() for the bindings before i (the failing binding itself is not rolled back), frees resp, sets the result code to SNMP_RET_ERR and jumps to the common exit. Phase 3 runs snmp_dep_commit; if it fails, error_status is its code and error_index is the last var_index (the last binding index, nbindings; 0 if there are no bindings); if snmp_dep_rollback then also fails and the PDU is not v1, error_status becomes SNMP_ERR_UNDO_FAILED and error_index 0; then rollback() is called for all nbindings bindings, resp is freed, the code becomes SNMP_RET_ERR and control goes to the common exit. Phase 4 calls each action with SNMP_OP_COMMIT (a failure is only logged); then snmp_fix_encoding is called and, if it does not return SNMP_CODE_OK, resp is freed and the code becomes SNMP_RET_IGN. The common exit (reached only from phases 2 to 4) calls snmp_dep_finish and returns the code, which is SNMP_RET_OK unless changed as above. The early returns of phase 1 do not pass through snmp_dep_finish (the dependency list is still empty at that point).
note: Reviewer: header-encoding failure returns IGN without freeing resp/error fields (right, snmpagent.c:681-682, already in prose). Round-15 claim 'dependency commit failure sets error_index 0' is only right when the dependency rollback also fails on a non-v1 PDU (lines 874-877); otherwise error_index is context.ctx.var_index. Old prose also wrongly said the failing binding index was used and that the dependency list is finished on every path reaching the common exit without distinguishing the phase-1 returns.

name: op_ifxtable
prose: Slice cut the head: this is the tail of op_ifxtable (defined at line 366), the handler for the ifXTable columns. Precondition: ctx and value are valid, sub is the number of OID sub-identifiers before the column, op is an snmp_op. GETNEXT returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME when there is no next interface, otherwise rewrites value->var to the next interface index; GET returns NOSUCHNAME if the instance suffix is not exactly one sub-identifier or the interface is unknown; SET returns SNMP_ERR_NO_CREATION for a bad suffix or unknown interface, SNMP_ERR_RES_UNAVAIL if snmp_dep_lookup fails, and for ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable and ifPromiscuousMode returns WRONG_VALUE unless the integer is 1 or 2, INCONS_VALUE if that field was already set in this request, otherwise records it in the dependency record and returns NOERROR; any other SET column returns NOT_WRITEABLE; ROLLBACK and COMMIT return NOERROR without doing anything. For GET and GETNEXT it calls mib_fetch_ifmib(ifp) (result ignored) when ifp->mibtick < this_tick and then fills value for the column: ifName and ifAlias use string_get (result NOERROR, or RES_UNAVAIL if malloc fails; ifAlias passes ifp->alias_size - 1 as the length), the multicast/broadcast/HC counters, ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable (1 or 2 from trap_enable), ifHighSpeed ((baudrate + 499999) / 1000000), ifPromiscuousMode (1 if IFF_PROMISC else 2), ifConnectorPresent (1 or 2) and ifCounterDiscontinuityTime (counter_disc - start_tick if counter_disc > start_tick, else 0) are stored in value->v; a column not in that switch leaves value unchanged and returns NOERROR.

name: op_snmp
prose: Handler for the mib-2 snmp group scalars; the leaf is value->var.subs[sub-1]. GETNEXT aborts the process (abort()). GET stores the value of the requested leaf (the counters in snmpd_stats, TRUTH_MK(snmpd.auth_traps) for snmpEnableAuthenTraps, silentDrops, proxyDrops) in value->v and returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR, and returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME for any other leaf. SET of snmpEnableAuthenTraps returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE without side effects if value->v.integer is not a valid truth value, otherwise saves value->v.integer in ctx->scratch->int1, sets snmpd.auth_traps from TRUTH_GET(value->v.integer) and returns NOERROR. ROLLBACK of that leaf assigns ctx->scratch->int1 (the saved integer as stored, not converted with TRUTH_GET) back to snmpd.auth_traps and returns NOERROR; COMMIT of that leaf returns NOERROR. A SET, ROLLBACK or COMMIT for any other leaf, and any other op value, reaches abort().
note: Round-15 reviewer right: GET with an unsupported leaf returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME (action.c default case), it does not abort as the old precondition claimed.

name: TestSpecParser::visitChar
prose: Precondition: none beyond the parser object being in a valid state. Postcondition: if c is a backslash and m_mode is not EscapedName it calls escape() (saves the current mode in lastMode, sets m_mode = EscapedName and pushes m_realPatternPos onto m_escapeChars), then addCharToPattern(c), which unconditionally appends c to m_substring and m_patternName and increments m_realPatternPos, and returns true. Otherwise, if c is ',' and m_mode is not EscapedName, it returns separate(): for QuotedName or Tag mode that sets m_mode = None, m_pos = m_arg.size(), clears m_substring and m_patternName and returns false; for any other mode it calls endMode(), addFilter() (which pushes the current filter if it has patterns) and returns true. Otherwise it dispatches on m_mode: None calls processNoneChar (a space returns true so the character is dropped; '~' sets m_exclusion; '[' starts Tag; '"' starts QuotedName; any other character starts Name; the last four continue below); Name calls processNameChar ('[' sets m_exclusion if m_substring is "exclude:" or else calls endMode(), then starts Tag); EscapedName calls endMode() (reverts to lastMode), addCharToPattern(c) and returns true; Tag, QuotedName and any other mode call processOtherChar, which returns false for a non-control character and, for a control character of the mode, appends c to m_substring, calls endMode() and returns true. If it did not return earlier it appends c to m_substring, appends c to m_patternName and increments m_realPatternPos only when c is not a control character of the (possibly new) mode, and returns true. So the only false result comes from separate().
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: addCharToPattern (catch.hpp:5184) unconditionally updates m_substring, m_patternName and m_realPatternPos; it does not skip control characters (that check is in the final lines of visitChar, not in the backslash branch). Prose kept, with the false-return condition made explicit.

name: operator << (ostream&, XmlEncode const&)
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: calls xmlEncode.encodeTo(os) and returns os. encodeTo walks m_str byte by byte and writes: '<' as < and '&' as &; '>' as > only when it has at least three characters before it and the two preceding characters are ']' (otherwise '>' unchanged); '"' as " only when the encoder was built ForAttributes (otherwise unchanged); bytes below 0x09, 0x0E to 0x1F and 0x7F as \xHH (uppercase, two hex digits, via hexEscapeChar, which saves and restores the stream's format flags but leaves the fill character '0'); other bytes below 0x7F unchanged (so tab, LF, VT, FF and CR pass through); for a byte of 0x80 or above it hex-escapes just that byte when it is below 0xC0 or at least 0xF8, when the multi-byte sequence would run past the end of the string, when a continuation byte does not match 10xxxxxx, when the decoded value is below 0x80, when it is in [0x80,0x800) but encoded in more than 2 bytes, when it is above 0x800 and below 0x10000 but encoded in 4 bytes, or when it is at least 0x110000; otherwise it copies the whole sequence unchanged. Because only the lead byte of a rejected sequence is escaped, the following bytes are examined on their own (continuation bytes then get escaped individually). The overlong test uses a strict '0x800 < value', so a 4-byte encoding of exactly U+0800 is not rejected, and surrogate values are not rejected.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the overlong check is (0x800 < value && value < 0x10000 && encBytes > 3), which misses value == 0x800 (catch.hpp:15245). The slice's operator<< itself only forwards to encodeTo.

name: value<T>
prose: Function template value<T>(T&& value) in Catch::Generators. Precondition: the argument is convertible to T, which is deduced as a forwarding reference; it is meant for rvalue arguments (T then a non-reference type). Postcondition: returns a GeneratorWrapper<T> owning (through a unique_ptr made by pf::make_unique) a newly allocated SingleValueGenerator<T> constructed from std::forward<T>(value); its get() returns the stored value and its next() always returns false, so exactly one value is produced. For an lvalue argument T would be an lvalue-reference type and the generator would hold a reference member (SingleValueGenerator stores T m_value), so the referent would have to outlive the wrapper; this function does not handle that case specially. Allocation or the copy/move of the argument may throw.
note: Unreviewed earlier; I qualified the lvalue case (the old prose said the stored reference is simply valid while the argument lives).

prose: Function template table<Ts...>(std::initializer_list<std::tuple<typename std::decay<Ts>::type...>> tuples). name: count_bits
prose: Function template test::detail::count_bits<A, a...>() (constexpr); it needs at least one character in the pack (an empty braced list cannot be deduced in the range-for). It scans the characters with a small mode machine starting in BIN mode, counting bits: in BIN mode spaces, tabs and newlines are ignored, ';' enters COMMENT mode, 'x' or 'X' enters HEX mode, '!' enters CHECK mode, '@' enters GOTO mode with addr = 0, '0', '1' and '.' each add one bit, and any other character throws the string "bad character"; COMMENT mode ends at a newline; HEX mode adds 4 bits per hex digit (throws "unaligned hex digit" if the bit count is not a multiple of 4), ignores ':' and returns to BIN on any other character; CHECK mode ignores digits and returns to BIN on any other character (the address is not checked here, so "address check failed" is never thrown by count_bits); GOTO mode accumulates decimal digits into addr and, on the first non-digit, throws "cannot go backwards" if 8*addr < bits, otherwise sets bits = 8*addr and returns to BIN. The inner 'again' loop is `for (bool again = true; again; again = false)`, so the again flag set by the helpers has no effect: the character that ends a HEX, CHECK or GOTO run is consumed by that step and is not reprocessed in BIN mode. A GOTO or CHECK still open at the end of the input has no effect. It returns the final bits count; the thrown string literals are the only error reporting (in a constant expression they make the program ill-formed).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: count_bits never calls handle_check, so it cannot throw "address check failed" (that is thrown by handle_check, used by constbuf()). Also noted from the code: the terminating character of hex/check/goto runs is consumed because 'again' is reset by the for-increment.

name: matching_vector
prose: Precondition: vector is a valid index into the static array order (0 <= vector < nentries); i = order[vector] is read first, and if i >= 2*nstates the function returns -1 before reading tally[i] or width[i]; otherwise tally[i], width[i], froms[i] and tos[i] must be valid, and for every earlier entry j = order[prev] that gets examined, tally[j], width[j], froms[j] and tos[j] must be valid and froms[j], tos[j] must hold at least tally[i] entries when width[j] and tally[j] equal width[i] and tally[i]. Postcondition: returns -1 if order[vector] >= 2*nstates; otherwise it scans prev = vector-1 down to 0 and returns -1 immediately at the first prev whose j = order[prev] has a different width or a different tally than i (it does not look at smaller prev); for a j with equal width and tally it compares tos[j][k] and froms[j][k] with tos[i][k] and froms[i][k] for k in [0, tally[i]) and returns j (the vector number order[prev], not prev) at the first full match, scanning from the nearest earlier entry; it returns -1 if the scan ends without a match. It only reads the static arrays order, tally, width, froms, tos and the global nstates; it allocates and frees nothing and modifies nothing.

name: copy_union
prose: Precondition: cptr points just after the %union token in the current input line (begin_ainfo records cptr-6 for diagnostics). If unionized is already set it calls over_unionized(), which prints an error and ends the program through done(1); otherwise it sets unionized = 1. Postcondition: through puts_both/putc_both it writes the guard lines '#ifdef YYSTYPE', '#undef  YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED', '#define YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED 1', '#endif', '#ifndef YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED', '#define YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED 1' to text_file (and also to union_file only when dflag is set), then a line-number directive to text_file only, then the union text. Identifier characters between %union and the first '{' are collected as a tag (at most NAME_LEN characters kept) and whitespace is buffered. At the opening brace, if a tag was found it writes 'union <tag>' plus the buffered whitespace, otherwise 'typedef union YYSTYPE' plus the whitespace; the union body is copied up to the brace that brings the depth back to 0, copying string and character literals and comments through copy_string and copy_comment and reading further lines with get_line. At the closing brace it writes '; ' and then 'typedef union <tag> YYSTYPE;' for the tagged case, or ' YYSTYPE;' (completing 'typedef union YYSTYPE {...} YYSTYPE;') for the untagged case, then '#endif /* !YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED */'. It leaves cptr just past the closing brace and returns nothing. If the input ends before the matching brace, unterminated_union() prints an error and ends the program through done(1).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: with a tag before '{' the code emits 'union <tag> {...}; typedef union <tag> YYSTYPE;' (reader.c:1013-1015, 1058-1067), so the union is not 'renamed to YYSTYPE'; the untagged case emits 'typedef union YYSTYPE {...} YYSTYPE;'. done() closes files and calls exit(k) (main.c:131-175).

name: YYPARSE_DECL()
prose: Generated LALR(1) parser driver (byacc skeleton). It is spelled YYPARSE_DECL() in the source and compiled as calc1_parse(void); it takes tokens from calc1_lex(&calc1_lval) and reports diagnostics through calc1_error(msg). Precondition: the generated constant parse tables of this file and the lexer/error functions it calls must exist; no other state has to be initialised by the caller, because the function sets its own error count, error flag, lookahead and start state at entry, and it keeps the error count, error flag, lookahead, semantic values and the stack in local variables (the stack structure is zeroed with memset at entry). Behaviour: it reads a token from the lexer only when no lookahead is pending (a negative lexer result is treated as end of input, token 0), shifts and reduces according to the tables, and runs the grammar's reduction actions. Its reduction actions belong to an interval/floating-point calculator grammar: they print with printf, update the dreg[] and vreg[] registers and call vmul, vdiv and dcheck; the action for an out-of-order interval and the actions that find a zero-containing divisor with dcheck jump to yyerrlab (the explicit-YYERROR behaviour described below). Syntax errors: when the tables report a conflict it starts or continues a trial parse (a copy of the stacks is saved in a state obtained from yyNewState and the lexemes read are queued in malloc/realloc'd buffers); an error inside a trial parse backtracks to the saved state. An error found when no trial parse is pending and the error flag is 0 calls calc1_error("syntax error") and increments the error count; an explicit YYERROR in an action pops the right-hand side of the rule being reduced and, when no trial parse is pending, enters recovery without calling the error function or incrementing the error count. In recovery (error flag 3) states are popped until one shifts the error token and lookahead tokens are discarded.
